ratings.reason: The architecture diagram misplaces Scan.jl under CLI/ (6-space indent matching CLI verbs) when it is actually a top-level src/Scan.jl include, so a reader using this diagram as a map would look in the wrong directory.

ARCHITECTURE.md documents rubric-audit.js and attack-design.js as delivered v1.0.0 contributions, but no CLI verb or launch site exists for either, so the doc's claim of a working, wired capability is stale/false.

Missing id-echo instructions in two scripts' prompts (unlike their fixed siblings) can cause a correctly-audited finding to be silently misclassified as a dead auditor, corrupting round data, though it requires the model to paraphrase the id rather than being guaranteed to occur.

The missing required-arg guard for 'round' is a real inconsistency with sibling scripts, but it is a latent robustness gap (fails silently only if 'round' is actually omitted by a caller), not a demonstrated live defect.

The docstring signature drops the AbstractString type on one argument versus the method's actual annotation — a localized, single-symbol slip with a correct sibling docstring right nearby in the same file, not a claim that misleads about behavior.

RULES.toml mislabels RULE.CIT.DOI's check as an unbuilt 'weakness' when a hard-tier scan already enforces it, contradicting the scan's own header and config, undermining the rulebook's self-reported coverage that RULE.TEST.RULE_WITH_CHECK exists to keep honest.

A reader of the rendered docs-rubric.md in isolation hits an ordering clause presupposing a `# Arguments` heading that RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM (the rubric's own rule for that section) forbids in favor of a prose lead-in, with no disclosed provenance for the discrepancy — a genuine contradiction between two normative statements in the same load-bearing, fleet-wide policy text, not just a stylistic wrinkle.

The unreachable `batches` branch and its header comment could mislead a reader of the script into thinking that mode is exercised, but the single real call site always hard-codes `mode: 'lanes'` so no actual run is affected — a localized, verifiable dead-code/documentation drift rather than a defect that changes any result a user sees.

Real inconsistency in empty-list guards across the eleven scripts against the package's own RULE.TEST.MISSING_IS_FAILING intent, but the finding itself states the gap looks unreachable under the current CLI's lane/hat resolution — a design-consistency gap with no demonstrated failure, not something a reader or user is likely to actually hit.
